newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs to set up new securities clearing house.
newsitem.headline: Czechs to set up new securities clearing house.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday that the finance ministry would open a tender in February in search of an organisation to manage a new securities clearing house.
The decision comes following years of criticism of the Czech share trading environment because of problems at the state-run Central Securities Registry (SCP).

"The finance ministry will call an open tender by the 15th of February for the opening of the clearing centre, so that test operation can start by the end of this year and real operations at the beginning of 1998," Klaus told reporters.
Speaking at a news conference after a meeting with Finance Ministry personnel about beefing up market supervision, Klaus said that the new clearing house would not necessarily replace the SCP.
He did not elaborate on what criteria would be used for selecting the organisation to run the clearing house.
Many investors, frustrated by a cumbersome Czech securities clearing system, have repeatedly called for a better system to expedite the closing of trades.
Under the current system the payment for trades is settled with the central bank, while the actual transfer of shares is settled by the SCP.

In December, government ministers agreed with capital market experts to move supervision of the securities' markets out of the finance ministry into a separate "Securities Bureau" which would eventually evolve into an independent body akin to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The new bureau, which in the interim, will still be managed by the finance ministry, is to open its new offices on February 1.
Klaus said that he was "satisfied with the strengthening of the activities of the (finance ministry) supervisor... it has been proven by the number of audits and sanctions during the last half year."
